title: Prenatal organochlorine and methylmercury exposure and memory and learning in school-age children in communities near the New Bedford Harbor Superfund site, Massachusetts.
ehr_evidence: The study used the New Bedford Cohort, a prospective birth cohort recruiting mother-infant pairs from St. Luke's Hospital (1993-1998); exposure was measured in cord serum (PCBs, DDE) and maternal hair mercury, and outcomes were assessed by neuropsychological testing, with only routine pediatric blood lead levels abstracted from medical records.
summary: A prospective birth cohort study of 393 school-age children (mean ~8 years, range 7-11) near a PCB-contaminated harbor in New Bedford, Massachusetts, examining associations of low-level prenatal PCB/DDE and methylmercury exposure with memory and learning (WRAML).
key_findings: Each 1 μg/g increase in maternal hair mercury was associated with decrements of -2.8 on Visual Memory (95% CI: -5.0, -0.6, p = 0.01), -2.2 on Learning (95% CI: -4.6, 0.2, p = 0.08), and -1.7 on Verbal Memory (95% CI: -3.9, 0.6, p = 0.14).
No significant adverse associations of ∑PCB4, dioxin-like PCBs, or DDE with WRAML memory and learning indices were observed.
After excluding three high-exposure outliers, the previously significant DDE-Learning association became essentially null.
Significant negative associations were found for the Finger Windows subtest (β = -0.49, 95% CI: -0.98, -0.01, p = 0.05) and Visual Learning subtest (β = -0.50, 95% CI: -1.01, 0, p = 0.05).
No significant interactions with sociodemographic variables were observed (all p for interaction > 0.05).
captured_features: WRAML Verbal Memory, Visual Memory, and Learning indices
WRAML subtests (Finger Windows, Visual Learning, Design Memory, etc.)

Covariates: child age, sex, race/ethnicity, birth year, birth weight, gestational age, school grade, parental education, household income, maternal IQ, prenatal omega-3 intake, OB risk score, HOME score, blood lead
pathologies_diseases: Memory and learning deficits (neurodevelopmental outcomes assessed by WRAML)
population: 393 school-age children (mean ~8 years, range 7-11) born 1993-1998 to mothers residing in towns surrounding the PCB-contaminated New Bedford Harbor, Massachusetts
exposure_domain: Environmental contaminants: organochlorines (PCBs, DDE) and heavy metals (methylmercury)
limitations: Null PCB findings may reflect lack of statistical power or a threshold/nonlinear dose-response at low exposure levels.
Selection bias: included children had higher maternal IQ, parental education, and breastfeeding rates than excluded children.
Hair mercury may be a less sensitive biomarker than blood, biasing associations toward the null.
Lack of individual cord serum lipid levels for lipid adjustment.
Only ~50% of the 8-year cohort had hair mercury measures and 393 had complete exposure/outcome/covariate data.
